scenario_overlay.labeling_authority: For this local queue, a medication-category aspirin AllergyIntolerance with no documented reaction phenotype is not cleared by an informal 'no drug allergy documented' line on a later specialty note. Current naproxen labeling specifically warns about aspirin-sensitive asthma and cross-reactivity; it does not establish that every generic aspirin-allergy entry has that phenotype. Under the conservative local workflow, when the allergy remains uncharacterized and no allergist exception is on file, do not label or dispense the refill. Place the request in pending-allergy-review, notify the prescriber, and do not discontinue the osteoarthritis plan.

decision_policy.rule: Local queue rule: if a medication-category aspirin AllergyIntolerance is active, its reaction phenotype is not documented, the queued product is naproxen, and no ticket-specific allergist exception is found, do not dispense from this queue. Route to pending allergy review and notify the prescriber. A specialty note that merely omits the allergy list does not clear the record. This workflow does not assert aspirin-sensitive asthma, and it does not discontinue osteoarthritis therapy.
